title: Animated Ad Agencies That Deliver Ads in Days, Not Weeks
summary: Compare animated ad agencies that deliver in days, with stated first-delivery times, animation types, prices and the approval steps that set the timeline.
body_markdown:
## Vidful and Adguns: fast weekly volume


[Vidful](https://vidful.co/) sells three monthly plans. Its lowest plan is 60 videos for $3,495 a month, built as 20 concepts with 3 hooks each, and Vidful says its entry plan ships 15 videos every week. The other two plans are 90 videos plus 110 statics for $5,400 and 120 videos plus 250 statics for $6,900. First creatives arrive by the end of week one, plans are billed monthly with no contracts, and revisions are unlimited. Vidful also lists a weekly ad performance review but does not say it manages ad accounts.


[Adguns](https://adguns.com/service/weekly-creatives/) describes 10 to 30 fresh concepts a week plus resizes, with static and animated ads and video edits among its formats. It starts from €1,000 a month, and its first batch typically ships within two weeks of kickoff. Media buying, landing pages and original video shoots are not included.


## What should you check before you trust a turnaround claim?


A first-batch date is only as reliable as the approval path behind it. Start by asking what the clock counts from: Knowlify and Adguns both count from kickoff, while Vidful's "end of week one" should be tied to a named start event in the quote. Then check how many revision rounds the quote includes, who approves each stage, which file formats you will receive and what happens if the script changes after animation starts. Vidful's unlimited revisions help only if they cover script changes, so confirm that in writing.


Check the format of the motion too. Meta's[guidance on turning still image ads into video](https://www.facebook.com/business/news/4-ways-to-turn-still-image-ads-into-video-ads) , published in 2018, suggests animating a still image with only one or two elements of motion in a few seconds, bringing the brand or key benefit to life, or using motion to show how the product works. The same page says Meta conducted 49 studies with brands using these production methods and saw a positive outcome for 69% of the brands. That supports light motion as a starting point, not a guarantee for your account. For the broader question, see[do animated ads work on Facebook and Instagram](https://knowlify.com/articles/do-animated-ads-work-on-meta) , and for a longer vendor list, our[best animated ad agencies guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/best-animated-ad-agencies) .


## Which placements and sound details should you ask for?


Ask for every placement size before the batch starts. Biddyco says its finished ads come in every placement size for Reels, Stories and Feed; with other providers, confirm that vertical and Feed exports are in the price, because a single master file may need a second export pass. Our[Facebook video ad specs guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/meta-video-ad-specs) covers the sizes in detail.


Sound is a separate approval. Biddyco's process treats sound and voiceover as a late stage, where it says AI speeds up the work. Ask who approves the voice, which music rights the file includes and whether a voiceover change restarts the animation. Those answers decide whether the first batch really arrives in days.


## Key takeaways


- Knowlify is our top pick for speed: its first batch lands five days after kickoff, and it delivers about 25 finished ads a week.
- Hand-built motion runs in stages, and each stage (brief, storyboard, animation, sound) adds time.
- Vidful and Adguns state first-delivery windows of about a week and two weeks, while Biddyco states two to four weeks.
- Confirm what the clock counts from, the revision rounds and the placement sizes before you trust any turnaround claim.
- Light motion has a published track record on still ads, but confirm it in your own account.


## FAQ


### Which animated ad agency delivers fastest?


Knowlify is our top pick for speed. Its first batch lands five days after kickoff, and it delivers about 25 finished ads a week across AI UGC, character animation and AI commercials. Vidful says first creatives arrive by the end of week one, and Adguns says its first batch ships within two weeks of kickoff.


### Is animation better than live-action UGC on Meta?


Meta's own evidence compares light motion with still images, not animation with live action. Animation earns its place when it makes one message clear in the first seconds. Test it against your current ads in your own account before you commit to a format.


### What does a motion ad batch cost?


Published prices vary. Vidful lists $3,495 a month for 60 videos, up to $6,900 for 120 videos plus 250 statics, Adguns starts from €1,000 a month, and Biddyco does not publish prices. Compare the offers on finished ads, placements and revision rounds, not on the headline monthly fee.


### Do unlimited revisions speed up delivery?


Not by themselves. Unlimited revisions remove a cost barrier, but each round still needs an approval, so the calendar depends on how quickly you answer. Vidful says its plans include unlimited revisions with no contracts. Confirm whether that covers script changes and placement re-exports before you count on it.
